the conservation of South American anuranas is a priority for the Atlantic Rainforest, the Tropical Andes, and the southern part of the Andes, and Uruguay, and that a large proportion of this biodiversity is not represented by the current protected area system.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Brazilian Atlantic Forest is a rich and rare cell for South American anurams, and that the southern part of the Andes and Uruguay are a poor and rare cell.

the most important conservation areas in South America for amphibians would be the Brazilian Atlantic Forest, the Tropical Andes, and the Chaco, while the southern part of the Andes and Uruguay should be considered as a priority region for the conservation of rare species.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of species richness and range size provides a rapid assessment tool to define large-scale conservation priorities.
a simultaneous consideration species richness and rarity patterns can provide a rapid assessment of biodiversity and can help define conservation priorities.
